lesson.scenario: Two writable replicas detect concurrent document edits with version-vector dominance and retain siblings until resolution.
entities: Exchanges values with their complete vectors
Retains concurrent versions instead of dropping one
Merges siblings and writes a causally newer value

steps.title: A writes independently
steps.narration: A changes the document to red and increments only its own component from {0,0} to {1,0}.
steps.outcome: A’s version causally descends from the common base.
steps.invariant: A local write increments A and preserves every observed remote component.

steps.title: B writes concurrently
steps.narration: Without seeing A, B changes the document to blue and increments {0,0} to {0,1}.
steps.outcome: Neither edit contains the other in its causal history.
steps.invariant: Independent writers cannot infer an order from wall-clock arrival time.

steps.title: Vectors compare as concurrent
steps.narration: Anti-entropy presents {1,0} and {0,1}; each is greater in one component and smaller in another.
steps.outcome: Both replicas retain two siblings rather than apply last arrival wins.
steps.invariant: Vector x dominates y only when every component is at least y and one component is greater.

steps.title: Resolver joins causal histories
steps.narration: A reader merges the content to purple, joins vectors to {1,1}, then writes at A by incrementing A to {2,1}.
steps.outcome: The resolution explicitly descends from both concurrent edits.
steps.invariant: A resolving write must join all sibling vectors before incrementing its writer component.

steps.title: Dominating resolution prunes siblings
steps.narration: B receives purple {2,1}; the comparator proves it dominates {1,0} and {0,1}, so both old siblings are removed.
steps.outcome: Both replicas converge without erasing an unobserved concurrent update.
steps.invariant: Only a dominating vector may replace all versions it causally includes.

production.scenario: A factory-device twin service replicates configuration between robot controllers on the shop floor and a cloud operations portal, using version vectors to detect concurrent edits before rollout.
components: Changes conveyor speed limits from the factory edge network
Lets operators edit the same device twin from headquarters
Compares cloud and edge revisions for each twin document
Holds concurrent twin branches that require operator judgment
Sends the resolved twin back to edge controllers after merge
flows: The factory controller syncs a local twin edit after working offline during a line-network outage.
An operator has already changed the same speed limit from the cloud portal while the controller was disconnected.
compare edge and cloud version vectors
The sync API uses version vectors to determine whether one side descends from the other or both changed independently.
If one branch clearly supersedes the other, the authoritative twin store is updated directly.
When neither vector dominates, the system preserves both edits and routes the twin into conflict review instead of guessing.
An operator resolves the concurrent edits and writes one merged twin back to the authoritative store.
push resolved twin to the factory edge
The final merged configuration is sent back to controllers so the cloud and factory floor converge on the same twin state.
